name: Eliel
overview: Eliel was a male member of the tribe of Benjamin, identified uniquely as the son of Shimei. The biblical record provides limited information about him beyond his lineage and tribal affiliation. His mention in Scripture is brief and specific, focused primarily on his genealogical placement.
namesAndTitles: The name Eliel means 'G-d is my G-d,' reflecting a personal acknowledgment of God's sovereignty. This proper name, recorded in 1 Chronicles 8:20, does not appear to have been given directly by God but carries a meaningful theological declaration.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Eliel as the son of Shema, establishing a clear father-son relationship within the tribe of Benjamin. Beyond this, there are no additional family connections noted in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Eliel's significance lies in his place within the genealogical records of the tribe of Benjamin, serving as a link in the lineage that preserves the heritage and identity of God's people. His mention underscores the importance of family lines in God's providential plan, as recorded in the historical books of the Old Testament. Though not prominent in narrative events, his inclusion affirms the faithfulness of God's covenant community through successive generations.
